tasks.title: Coordinate pending requests and receiving-agent delivery
tasks.description: G-3, G-4, REQ-006, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-012, REQ-028, REQ-029, REQ-037, REQ-038, REQ-039, FR-1, FR-2, FR-4, FR-8, FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-12, DR-5, REQ-044, REQ-045, REQ-046, REQ-047, REQ-048, REQ-056, PR-1, PR-2, PR-3, AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-5, AC-6, AC-7, AC-8, AC-9, AC-10, and AC-11 / Component: Realtime coordination, correlation, and receiver delivery - add getAISummaryCorrelation with the exact {conversationId, interactionId} return shape (conversationId = mainInteractionId ?? interactionId; interactionId = the task's top-level interactionId) and a package-internal AISummaryCoordinator implementing the narrow request-coordinator interface. TaskManager lifecycle-owns one coordinator and both FR-11/FR-8 timer policies, while AISummaryCoordinator directly owns pendingAISummaryRequests, receivingSummaryBuffer, interactionFeatureEnablement, and all timer handles. Arm the request timer only with accepted pending insertion and the receiver timer only with buffer insertion/replacement; clear either through removeTimedEntry before settlement, cancellation, timeout, replacement, delivery, expiry, task cleanup, or SDK cleanup. Preserve the semantic aliases backed by the single AI_SUMMARY_DURATION_MS value, exact validated event-type correlation, timeout/overlap/late-event outcomes, latest-only buffering, ambiguity protection, and scoped/full cleanup. For a valid subsequent-agent payload with zero or multiple matching registered tasks, routeReceivingSummary replaces the per-conversation buffer with the latest payload and arms/rearms its 30-second timer. After TaskManager inserts or updates a task and emits its incoming/hydrate lifecycle event, it recomputes the candidate set and calls flushReceivingSummary; exactly one candidate makes the coordinator clear the buffer/timer before one delivery, while zero or multiple candidates retain it. Delivery, expiry, scoped task cleanup, and full SDK cleanup all remove receiver state through the same private removeTimedEntry helper; task removal and SDK deregistration both reach that path. TaskManager remains the raw double-envelope parser and task-registry owner, holds the current profile-derived ConfigFlags view, exposes the bound getGeneratedSummaryFlags accessor injected into every Task, composes exactly one coordinator for its own lifetime, derives complete conversation-matching task candidate sets, and delegates only validated payloads/state transitions while preserving transcript and suggested-response routing. Key pending requests by conversationId plus inbound summary type because FR-9 exposes no task/request identifier; store taskId only as an ownership guard, so cancellation and per-task cleanup are no-ops for a sibling owner's entry. Treat CONSULT and TRANSFER as one MID_CALL_SUMMARY slot despite their distinct outbound names. Count every parsed frame classified as FEATURE_ENABLEMENT once before payload validation, including repeated and payload-invalid frames; forward/store only valid payloads and exclude unparseable or unclassifiable frames from that metric. Store every valid feature payload and emit AGENT_EVENTS.FEATURE_ENABLEMENT through TaskManager's EventEmitter without importing ContactCenter. Emit AI_SUMMARY_INBOUND_EVENT_DROPPED exactly once with a bounded reason for each malformed, unknown, late, or uncorrelated summary frame, without double-counting classified invalid feature frames. For malformed, late, uncorrelated, and buffered receiver input, log or metric only bounded event/outcome metadata and never summary text, section values, Adaptive Card bodies, raw envelopes, or arbitrary exception text. Add direct AISummaryCoordinator fake-timer tests for the exact request/buffer arm points, resolver, overlap, owner cleanup, feature state, buffer-on-miss, replacement, registration-triggered flush/delivery, expiry, scoped/full buffer cleanup, ambiguity, privacy, shared-duration boundaries, exact exported timeout/overlap codes, and no stale timers on every cleanup path; keep TaskManager tests focused on parsing, validation, delegation, candidate selection, flush after task registration/listener availability, proof that legacy initiator aliases are never emitted, metrics, lifecycle integration, and regressions; retain TaskUtils correlation tests. This task owns REQ-056 timeout, unknown-task, malformed-event, and late-event behavior and the named AC state/RTD assertions. It depends only on contract types so it can proceed independently of HTTP transport.
tasks.acceptance: nvm use 22.14 && yarn workspace @webex/contact-center test:unit --targets services/task/TaskUtils.ts && yarn workspace @webex/contact-center test:unit --targets services/task/AISummaryCoordinator.ts && yarn workspace @webex/contact-center test:unit --targets services/task/TaskManager.ts
